title: ModelForms: Forms from Models
description: Create forms directly from your models to save time.

slides.title: Why ModelForm? 🤝
slides.content: If you have a model and want a form to create or edit instances, `ModelForm` automatically generates fields based on the model's fields. It handles validation and saving.

slides.title: Creating a ModelForm
slides.content:
Assume you have a `Post` model:
```python
from django.db import models

class Post(models.Model):
    title = models.CharField(max_length=200)
    content = models.TextField()
    author = models.ForeignKey(User, on_delete=models.CASCADE)
```

Define a ModelForm:
```python
from django.forms import ModelForm
from .models import Post

class PostForm(ModelForm):
    class Meta:
        model = Post
        fields = ['title', 'content']  # or '__all__'
        # exclude = ['author']  # alternative
```

The form will have fields `title` and `content` with appropriate widgets and validation from the model.

quizData.question: What is the main advantage of using a ModelForm over a regular Form?
options: It automatically saves the object to the database
It automatically generates fields based on a model and handles saving
It doesn't require a CSRF token
quizData.explanation: ModelForm saves time by inferring field definitions from a model and provides a `save()` method to create/update database records.

slides.title: Using ModelForm in a View
Pro Tip 💡
slides.content:
## Use `fields = '__all__'` carefully

It includes all model fields, which may expose sensitive fields. Always specify the fields you want users to edit.
